thread:
emma_support: FYI customer reports bursts of very high p99 and duplicate billing. They see requests go to us-east-1 then eu-west-1 within the same logical attempt. Started after SDK 0.9.3 rollout yesterday. Logs attached.

customer_qa: pasted snippet from customer (redacted):
```
2025-11-11T21:02:13Z request_id=abc123 region=us-east-1 sent
2025-11-11T21:02:13Z request_id=def456 region=eu-west-1 sent
2025-11-11T21:02:13Z response_from=eu-west-1 latency=420ms tokens=120 billed=true
2025-11-11T21:02:14Z response_from=us-east-1 latency=1.9s tokens=120 billed=true
```

customer_qa: SDK config they used:
```json
{ "mode": "hedged", "regions": ["us-east-1","eu-west-1"], "timeout_ms": 300, "backoff_ms": 50 }
```

rajesh_sdk: Hmm. Hedged mode concurrently issues requests to multiple regions. Expected behavior: first response wins and second should be cancelled server-side. If cancellations aren't propagated then both hits may execute and bill. Does the customer show two separate billing entries?

customer_qa: Yes, they have two billing lines for the same user request. Billing team confirmed double charge traces aligned with those two request_ids.

oliver_infra: I'll check routing changes. I see we rolled out an ingress fallback rule at 2025-11-12T02:10Z that will retry to alternate region on 5xx; that combined with client hedge could cause both requests to be accepted instead of cancelling the loser. Pulling router traces now.

sre_bot: deploy-bot: routing-policy/alt-region-fallback v1.3 deployed by @oliver_infra at 2025-11-12T02:10Z.

oliver_infra: Router trace example (excerpt):
```
incoming request client-id=x, route->us-east-1 accepted, fallback->eu-west-1 attempted after no early response. Both forwarded to serving cluster; serving did not terminate the second connection when first responded.
```

rajesh_sdk: Can you share a minimal repro we can run? Also which SDK call surface they used (generate/chat/embeddings)?

customer_qa: Repro steps provided by customer:
1) SDK 0.9.3 with hedged mode enabled and region list [us-east-1, eu-west-1]
2) call generate(prompt ~2k tokens) with timeout 300ms
3) observe two request IDs in logs, ~1st completes ~400ms, 2nd completes ~1.9s

rajesh_sdk: Repro snippet we used locally:
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(region='us-east-1', hedged=True, regions=['us-east-1','eu-west-1'], timeout_ms=300)
resp = client.generate(prompt='x'*2000)
print(resp.text)
```

rajesh_sdk: Quick analysis: options here - (A) change serving to cancel loser requests via an RPC cancel token when first response generated, (B) route hedged client requests back to a single region using sticky session affinity at ingress, or (C) change SDK to stop multi-region concurrent hedging by default and add idempotency header so billing side can dedupe.

oliver_infra: I've created INC-5432 and attached router traces. Short-term mitigation: revert alternate-region fallback or make it conditional on non-hedged clients. I'll roll a canary to reduce cross-region forwarding for hedged traffic.

rajesh_sdk: We'll prepare SDK patch 0.9.4: disable multi-region hedged by default and introduce X-Idempotency-Key header for generate calls. Also add explicit cancelation propagation: client sends request GUID that servers can use to cancel outstanding work. We'll push a canary to 10% of users.

emma_support: Can billing confirm whether dedupe by idempotency key will fix historic double charges or only prevent future ones?

sre_bot: billing-bot: queued for triage, case BILL-789. Dedupe post-hoc will require manual crediting for prior hits.

customer_qa: Customer tested disabling multi-region hedged; p99 dropped from 1.8s to 220ms and no duplicate billing observed in 30 mins of load. They're happy with workaround for now.

rajesh_sdk: We'll fast-track 0.9.4 canary and coordinate with infra to enable cancel signals. Follow-ups: #INC-5432 (infra), #SDK-1022 (client patch), #BILL-789 (billing credits).

emma_support: Thanks team. I'll update the customer and keep thread open while canary runs. :thumbsup:
